response.query: Which placebo outcomes best test exclusion restrictions for anchor‑LP shock instruments?
response.answer: Placebo outcomes testing for exclusion restrictions in anchor-LP shock instruments typically involve analyzing outcomes unrelated to the instrument's effect. Common tests include employment status and work participation outcomes. These help validate the instrument's exclusion restriction.

results.title: Frontiers | Initial estimates of the minimal clinically important difference for the Neuropathic Pain Symptom Inventory: a systematic meta-analysis
results.content: # Initial estimates of the minimal clinically important difference for the Neuropathic Pain Symptom Inventory: a systematic meta-analysis. The Neuropathic Pain Symptom Inventory (NPSI) is a commonly used assessment in neuropathic pain (NP) trials, yet a Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) has not been established. Four distributional approaches were applied to estimate the MCID: 1) meta-regression on the set of standard deviation (SD) of change scores, 2) meta-regression on the set of baseline SD scores, 3) simple aggregation on the set of SD of change scores, and 4) simple aggregation on the set of baseline SD scores. Control arms were examined separately in a sensitivity analysis using the simple aggregation method for both SD of change and baseline SD sets. The calculated MCID estimates for the NPSI total score (range 1–100) were 6.21 for the SD of change meta-regression and 7.1 for baseline SD meta regression. Control arms had a MCID of 8.04 for SD of Change and 8.71 for Baseline SD.
